cases.input:
Can you read this and tell me if I should sign it? A conference sent it over before I speak.

SPEAKER AGREEMENT
Between Northbeam Security Summit LLC ("Organizer") and the Speaker, for the event held 12-14 March at the Example Convention Center.

1. Organizer will provide one night of hotel and economy airfare, reimbursed within 90 days of receipts being submitted. Receipts submitted after 30 days of the event are not reimbursed.
2. Speaker grants Organizer a perpetual, worldwide, irrevocable, sublicensable license to record, edit, and distribute the session and all slides, in any media now known or later developed, including for commercial training products, without further payment.
3. Speaker will not present substantially similar material at any other event within 6 months before or 12 months after the Event.
4. Organizer may cancel at any time for any reason; if Organizer cancels, no expenses already incurred by Speaker are reimbursed.
5. If Speaker cancels for any reason other than a documented medical emergency, Speaker will pay a fee of USD 2,500.
6. Speaker will indemnify Organizer against all claims arising from the content of the talk, including third-party IP claims.
7. This agreement is governed by the laws of Delaware; disputes go to binding arbitration at Organizer's chosen venue, with the Speaker paying half the costs.
cases.expects: An ideal answer reads the agreement for what actually binds the principal and surfaces the real gotchas: a one-sentence summary, the key callouts, issues ranked by severity (critical, important, other), and a concrete change request to the sender for each critical and important issue. It cites only what the text says, in plain exact words, and does not pad with generic contract advice.

cases.input:
ok this is a mess, my contractor pasted pieces of the consulting agreement from three emails plus his notes. is there anything bad in here?? i need an answer fast

---fwd 1---
...Consultant's Work Product shall be deemed work made for hire, and to the extent not, Consultant hereby assigns all right, title and interest, including Consultant's Pre-Existing Tools as incorporated... [rest cut off]

---fwd 2--- (his note: "legal said this part is standard, ignore")
Fees: USD 18,000 per month. Client shall pay within net-15. See Schedule B for rates. [Schedule B not included]
Termination: either party may terminate with 60 days notice, except that during the Initial Phase Client may not terminate for convenience.
"Initial Phase" has the meaning in Exhibit A.

---fwd 3---
Non-solicit: for 24 months after termination Consultant shall not provide services to any customer of Client or any customer of Client's Affiliates, whether or not Consultant had contact with them. "Affiliates" includes any entity under common control with Client now or in the future.

my notes: they said they'd send the real doc friday, this is basically it. Sig block says Example Holdings Ltd, 203.0.113.0 is their office lol
cases.expects: The input is partial, unsigned-state excerpts with missing schedules and exhibits, and a note telling the reader to ignore a clause. An ideal answer still delivers the full pattern output from what is present, flags the IP assignment of pre-existing tools, the broad non-solicit and undefined Initial Phase as risks, and names what is missing (Schedule B, Exhibit A, the rest of the assignment clause) without inventing terms or deferring to the 'standard' claim.
